column3: NASB follows the critical text (“from God”) without “authorities” in the second clause; “being above” is rendered “governing,” and “instituted” is “established.”
NASB renders “has resisted” as “has opposed” and “judgment” as “condemnation.”
NASB follows the critical text; “a terror” is rendered “a cause of fear,” “the good work” is “good behavior,” and “from him” is “from the same.”
NASB refers to the authority as “it”; “servant” is rendered “minister,” and “in vain” is “for nothing.” It adds “who brings.”
NASB renders “on account of the conscience” as “for conscience' sake.”
NASB adds “rulers” and renders “attending continually” as “devoting themselves.”
NASB follows the critical text; “revenue” is rendered “custom,” and “respect” is “fear.” A full-width colon appears in the NASB text.
NASB follows the critical text without “You shall not bear false witness”; the quotations are in capitals.
NASB follows the critical text (“you”); it adds “do” and renders “first believed” as “believed.”
NASB follows the critical text; “nearly over” is rendered “almost gone,” and “works” is “deeds.”
NASB renders “walk” as “behave,” “reveling” as “carousing,” “sexual immorality” as “sexual promiscuity,” and “dissension” as “strife.”
